title: Aura
tagline: Dress confidently without sight — AI + RFID wardrobe assistant
summary: Built a custom AI model and RFID-powered system that helps visually impaired users independently select matching outfits for any occasion. Honored by Microsoft APAC and presented to the President Director of Microsoft Indonesia.
problem:
Blind and visually impaired individuals face a daily challenge most people never consider — getting dressed. Without the ability to visually verify outfit combinations, they depend on memorisation or sighted assistance, limiting their independence.

Aura solves this by pairing RFID-tagged clothing with HarmonyAI, a custom-built model that analyses color profiles, pattern compatibility, and occasion suitability to recommend complete outfits. The phone's built-in NFC reader identifies each garment instantly, and voice-first interaction guides the user through every step.

The project was recognised by Microsoft APAC, presented to Microsoft Indonesia leadership, and received Azure cloud credits for backend infrastructure.
features: HarmonyAI — custom model that scores color match between 2+ garments and generates a color profile
RFID tag reader via phone's built-in NFC to identify garments from a closet
Voice-first interaction with full screen reader accessibility
Wardrobe registration flow with audio confirmations
Microsoft Azure pipeline for model storage, data processing, and scalability
learnings: Designing UX for non-visual users fundamentally shifts every assumption — haptic feedback, audio cues, and sequential navigation replace visual hierarchy entirely.
Training a color-compatibility model required building a custom dataset of outfit pairings rated by fashion professionals.
Bridging native NFC/RFID hardware events into Flutter via platform channels taught low-level platform integration.
Presenting to Microsoft leadership sharpened the ability to distill a technical product into a compelling business narrative.

title: Visio
tagline: Real-time object detection that teaches children to see with sound
summary: An AI-powered learning companion that uses live camera object detection, ChatGPT integration, and gamified lessons to help visually impaired and curious children explore and understand the world around them.
problem:
Inclusive education tools for blind children remain scarce and often lack engagement. Children learn best through play and curiosity, yet most assistive apps offer static, limited experiences.

Visio turns a phone camera into a real-time learning companion — it detects objects, narrates what the child encounters, and reinforces understanding through interactive games. With ChatGPT integration, children can ask open-ended questions about any detected object, expanding their knowledge beyond pre-programmed content.

Flutter Isolates (multithreading) ensure the AI detection runs on a separate thread, keeping the UI buttery smooth even during continuous camera inference.
features: Real-time object detection using TensorFlow Lite with COCO dataset
Flutter Isolates for multithreaded processing — AI inference separated from UI logic
ChatGPT integration for open-ended Q&A about detected objects
Learn Braille mode with haptic feedback for tactile alphabet learning
Two-player online game mode via Firebase for social learning
Audio narration with adjustable pace
learnings: Running continuous ML inference on mobile requires isolating compute from the UI thread — Flutter Isolates made this practical without native code.
Integrating a conversational AI (ChatGPT) alongside real-time detection created a 'curiosity loop' that kept children engaged far longer than static content.
Designing haptic-only Braille lessons taught the importance of non-visual feedback channels in accessibility design.
Building a multiplayer game with Firebase Realtime Database required careful state synchronisation across devices.

title: Tukerin
tagline: Find, swap, and go — battery exchange network for EV motorcycles
summary: A location-based mobile app that helps Indonesian EV motorcycle riders locate nearby Battery Swap Stations, navigate with custom routing, and swap batteries instantly — featuring a C2C model where anyone can register as a station. Published in IEEE.
problem:
Indonesia's transition to electric vehicles is stalled by a single pain point — charging takes hours, and charging infrastructure is sparse. Battery swapping is the fastest alternative, but stations are few and their locations are hard to discover.

Tukerin introduces a customer-to-customer (C2C) model: any EV user can register their home or shop as a Battery Swap Station, similar to how food delivery platforms let small restaurants go online. This allows the BSS network to grow organically without heavy capital investment.

The app uses the Haversine formula for precise distance calculation and custom Google Maps navigation to route riders directly to the nearest available station.
features: Live BSS map with real-time availability powered by Google Maps API
Haversine formula for accurate distance calculation between rider and stations
Custom navigation paths with turn-by-turn routing
C2C station registration — any EV user can become a BSS operator
Trip history and cost tracking
learnings: Implementing the Haversine formula from scratch deepened understanding of geospatial math and its edge cases near the poles and the antimeridian.
Designing a C2C marketplace requires trust signals — user ratings, verification badges, and transaction history became essential for BSS credibility.
Writing and co-authoring an IEEE publication sharpened technical writing skills and taught the peer review process.
Custom polyline rendering on Google Maps required decoding route geometry and handling API rate limits gracefully.

title: Manu
tagline: Connecting small businesses with shared manufacturing capacity
summary: An e-commerce-style platform that helps Indonesian SMEs discover and book shared factory capacity, reducing the capital barrier to manufacturing and enabling small businesses to scale production without owning a factory.
problem:
Indonesia's SME (UMKM) sector boomed after COVID-19, but survival rates remain low — the primary bottleneck is insufficient capital for production. Most small business owners can't afford to build or lease a factory, yet their products need manufacturing at scale.

Manu is a first-of-its-kind platform that matches SMEs with available shared factories based on their product category and location. Think of it as an online food delivery model applied to manufacturing — factories register their idle capacity, and SMEs book production runs through the app.

With category and location filters, SMEs can find the right factory in minutes instead of months of networking.
features: Factory discovery with category and location-based filtering
E-commerce-style booking flow for manufacturing capacity
MVVM architecture for clean separation of concerns
Firebase backend with SQLite for offline-first local persistence
Factory registration portal for supply-side onboarding
learnings: Building with MVVM on native Android taught the discipline of separating UI from business logic — a pattern that transferred directly to every later project.
Designing an offline-first architecture with SQLite + Firebase sync required careful conflict resolution strategies.
A two-sided marketplace needs supply before demand — onboarding factories first proved critical for initial traction.

title: Tanivest
tagline: Micro-investment platform to save Indonesia's shrinking farmland
summary: A crowd-investing mobile app that pools micro-investments from everyday users to fund smallholder farm projects, tackling the capital shortage that causes 150,000+ hectares of Indonesian agricultural land to be abandoned annually.
problem:
Indonesia is an agricultural nation — the sector contributed 13.86% of national GDP between 2010–2016, and the government allocates an average of 31.24% of the state budget to support it. Yet 150,000 hectares of farmland disappear every year, equivalent to 300,000 tons of lost production.

The root cause is capital. Farmers lack the funds to maintain efficiency, profits drop, and landowners convert to more lucrative industries. Tanivest addresses this by letting everyday investors fund farm projects in small amounts, democratising agricultural investment while giving farmers the capital they need to keep land productive.
features: Browseable list of investable farm projects with yield projections
Interactive charts and graphs for portfolio tracking
Yield tracking and payout history per investment
KYC onboarding with secure authentication
learnings: Visualising financial data with interactive charts requires careful attention to axis scaling and update frequency to avoid misleading users.
Building a FinTech product taught the importance of trust UI — clear transaction histories, verified badges, and transparent fee structures.
Working on a socially impactful product (preserving farmland) provided strong motivation and a compelling narrative for stakeholder presentations.

title: Infarm
tagline: Fair-priced farm inputs marketplace built for non-tech-savvy farmers
summary: An e-commerce platform purpose-built for Indonesian farmers — with simplified UX, subcategory-based navigation, and direct seller messaging — to break vendor monopolies on farm input pricing caused by post-COVID supply disruptions.
problem:
COVID-19 disrupted farm input supply chains across Indonesia, leaving farmers at the mercy of local monopolies with inflated prices. Most farmers lack connections to alternative vendors and have no way to compare pricing.

Infarm was built with a critical constraint in mind: many Indonesian farmers are not fluent with technology. The UX prioritises simplicity — subcategory filters help users find exactly what they need (seeds, fertiliser, equipment), and a direct-message-with-seller feature enables price negotiation, replicating the trusted in-person haggling experience in a digital format.
features: Multi-vendor product catalogue with subcategory-based filtering
Direct message with seller for negotiation and inquiry
GetX state management for optimised performance and scalability
Lazy loading for handling large product queries efficiently
Cart, order tracking, and purchase history
learnings: Designing for non-tech-savvy users forced radical simplification — every extra tap is a potential drop-off point.
Implementing lazy loading for paginated product queries significantly improved perceived performance on low-end devices.
GetX state management proved effective for rapid prototyping but required discipline to avoid over-coupling controllers.
